actions.native: public unsafe void Dam_EnemyDamageBase.InstantDead(bool force = false)
actions.readback: the call answers nothing, so the commit is confirmed by reading Enemies.EnemyAgent.Alive back on the same resolved life; a life that still reads alive is an unknown commit, never a claimed one
actions.host: the receiver is reached through the module's own tracked instance, so the target is a `gtfo.enemy` life this provider answers for; the module's own CanExecute gate (registration + startup state + session flag + SNet.IsMaster) refuses a client before any write

native: public unsafe static NavMarkerLayer GuiManager.NavMarkerLayer (getter/setter on the static property)
public unsafe NavMarker NavMarkerLayer.PlaceCustomMarker(NavMarkerOption type, GameObject trackingObj, string name, float destroyDelay = 0f, bool debug = false)
actions.option: NavMarkerOption.EnemyTitleDistance (= EnemyDistance | Title = (Distance|Enemy)|Title) is the style the game's own enemy tag uses, so a Forge mark is the same icon, distance and title
actions.color: NavMarker.SetColor is the only colour entry in the build, and NavMarker has no public colour getter: the write is the confirmation, and the row's readback is the marker instance the layer returned
actions.duration: the row's `duration` is plan ticks; Forge owns the lifetime (the marker is placed with destroyDelay 0 and removed by the frame pump at the recorded tick), because the native marker carries no caller-set timer
actions.no-vanilla-tag: ToolSyncManager.WantToTagEnemy is not called: the vanilla tag accepts neither a colour nor a caller-set duration, so it is left alone (ruling 86/89, ni-markcolor.md route A)
actions.tier: `execution: presentation` (ruling 122.3). `GuiManager.NavMarkerLayer` is per-process state, so the marker can only be built on the machine that shows it: the host decides the step, its timing and the audience, and each addressed player runs the handler on its own machine. The audience is the realm's own player list (`EnemyModule.PresentationAudience` over `SNet.SessionHub.PlayersInSession`), registered as this provider's one `PresentationSessions` entry. The handler reports a non-committing result, which is what the tier requires and what a marker local to a screen really is.

native: public unsafe bool Enemies.EnemyAgent.PropagateTargetLimited(Agents.Agent targetAgent, float chanceToPropagate)
actions.lookup: the player agent is read from the game's own id table (`Agents.AgentManager.GetAgent(int gid, out Agent agent)` / `GetAgent<T>(int gid, out T agent) where T : Agent`), the same inverse the weapon package's mark adapter uses; a reference the kind's provider does not answer for is refused before the call
actions.readback: the limited form answers whether the propagation was kept, which is reported as `propagated`; the full form returns void and its confirmation is the surviving life and the resolved instance

values.read: ForgeRuntime ObservationContracts reads RuntimeEntitySnapshot.Health / HealthMaximum and derives fraction for gtfo.player | gtfo.enemy.
values.producer: ForgeEnemy/Native/Observation/EnemyEntityObserver.cs publishes the enemy health pair into the shared snapshot; ForgeEnemy no longer owns a duplicate health query row.

values.read: GameData.EnemyDataBlock.persistentID through Enemies.EnemyAgent.EnemyData, both read back after the getter ran
RuntimeEntitySnapshot.AiState == "hibernating" (a member of the shared ai_state set)
values.producer: the same observer's own EB_States -> ai_state table; the two native members it maps to hibernation are EB_States.Hibernating (0) and the squid boss's own hibernation (12), the same pair forge.trigger.enemy.awakened treats as the sleeping baseline

values.read: RuntimeEntitySnapshot.Position plus RuntimeQuerySession.TryZone, which answers through this provider's registered EntityZones responder (AIG_CourseNode.m_zone -> AIG_Layer.m_type / dimension / local index)
values.gap: the kernel reports `entity-zone-unknown` when the responder answers null, so a provider cannot tell `this entity stands in no zone` from `I could not place it`. The row answers the zone port as null in both cases; a kernel seam that distinguishes the two is a request in this slice's integration.json

notImplemented.reason: ES_Hibernate exposes no readable heartbeat member in this build: the interop type carries no public counter, event or field that changes per beat, and the native dump shows no timer this package may read. No forced implementation and no invented state.
